title: Constant-time deterministic dynamic dictionaries
formal: For every fixed integer \(c\ge2\), does there exist a uniform deterministic word-RAM dictionary with capacity \(N\), word size \(w=\lceil c\log_2(N+2)\rceil\), \(O(N)\) words of space, \(O(1)\) worst-case lookup time and \(O(1)\) amortized insertion and deletion time? The guarantees must hold for every valid online sequence on \(w\)-bit keys and values, starting empty, after \(O(N)\) initialization.
definitions: A uniform sequential word RAM has a fixed finite program, word-sized registers and addressed memory cells. Unit-cost instructions are reads and writes, comparisons, branching, addition, subtraction, multiplication, integer division with nonzero divisor, Boolean bit operations and logical shifts. Arithmetic stored in one word is modulo \(2^w\); shifts by at least \(w\) yield zero. Addresses must fit the available word size. All table construction and input-dependent auxiliary memory count; there is no free advice or input-dependent oracle. Randomized programs may generate independent uniform random words. The program receives \(N\ge2\) and \(w\). Insert supplies a new key and a value, Delete names a present key, and Lookup returns its value or an absent marker. At most \(N\) keys are simultaneously stored. No random instruction is allowed in this deterministic target. For each fixed \(c\), constants may depend on \(c\) but not on \(N\), input keys or sequence length. The joint amortized bound is total cost \(O(N+q+u)\) for \(q\) queries and \(u\) updates, while every query individually costs \(O(1)\). All retained input information, including any direct-address table, counts toward the \(O(N)\) space bound. This logarithmic-word, fixed-capacity formulation asks already for constant amortized updates; it does not demand constant worst-case updates.
why: This is a basic possible separation between the power of randomization and determinism in a general-purpose data-structure primitive.

context_blocks.text: Randomized hashing provides constant lookup and expected amortized update guarantees in linear space. Pătrașcu identifies superconstant deterministic dictionary lower bounds as a research direction pursued with Thorup.

The dynamic target differs from constructing a static dictionary once: rebuilding, deletion and repeated adversarial changes must all fit the same operation budget. The related static construction card is retained separately.

answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the stated existence claim or its logical negation, with the same inputs, computation model, space allowance, quantifiers and cost guarantees. A result for a restricted input family or a different model does not decide the full target.
status_note: Open in the cited dated sources. The bounded source and subsequent-result review on 13 September 2026 found no verified resolution of this target; this is not exhaustive certification of current openness.

notes: A concrete logarithmic-word, linear-capacity-space version of the broad deterministic dictionary problem. Constant amortized updates with worst-case lookups are requested; this is not silently strengthened to worst-case constant updates.

sentences: A dynamic dictionary maintains key-value records under insertion and deletion.
Hashing gives constant expected operation bounds using random choices.
The question asks for the same basic performance from deterministic programs.
The space budget excludes a table covering the entire key universe.
Either such an implementation or a general impossibility result would clarify the value of randomization.
